newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Jan 9.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Jan 9.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Popular Australian jockey Jim Cassidy returned to the winners mount yesterday after 20 months in the wilderness after his involvement in the Jockey Tapes scandal. It was Cassidy's first win in 18 rides and it was greeted with a huge ovation from the Canterbury crowd. Page 20.

World No. 1 tennis player Pete Sampras sent an ominous warning to his competitors yesterday after a convincing win against Michael Stich in the Colonial Classic at Kooyong. The win began Sampras' quest for the Australian Open, which he is determined to wn after last year's loss to Australian star, Mark Philippoussis. Page 20.

Australian Tennis player Patrick Rafter won a berth into the quarter finals of the Sydney International yesterday after eliminating No. 8 seed, Paul Haarhuis. Rafter, who spent much of 1996 frustrated by injury attributed his win to a more relaxed attitude on big points. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Questions have begun to be asked about the performance of new Australian cricket coach Geoff Marsh following the team's recent poor form. Australia's one-day slump has seen it win only two of its last twelve matches, which has led to doubts about Marsh'scredentials. Page 48.

Jacques Villeneuve, runner up in last year's Formula One racing championship, has ruled out the chances of defending champion Damon Hill. Villeneuve said that 1997 will be his year, and that Hill's TWR Arrows team is not ready to win the championship. Page 49.

There is still some doubt as to which Australian golf course will host the 1998 Presidents Cup against the US. Eight courses have so far been inspected, and State Premiers Bob Carr and Jeff Kennett have made great attempts to woo golf officials to their respective States. Page 49.
THE AGE

The Victorian Cricket Association is set reduce the size of the MCG for next year's one day series, in an attempt to make the ground more conducive to one day cricket. The proposed changes come in the wake of the successful one day match at the GABBA in risbane last weekend, where 565 runs were scored during the day. Page B8.

The ACB has been criticised for its part in the Australian cricket team's recent poor form. There have been calls to reduce the number of national selectors from the current number of five, to a smaller, more workable number. Page B8.

The finals of the soccer Peace Cup in Somalia have ended in violence, as one of the players opened fire at a rival team. After a goal was disallowed and the referee knocked out, a disgruntled player fired at his opponents with a machine gun, for five mintes. No one was hurt in the incident. Page B8.
THE HERALD SUN

Senior Australian cricket players Ian Healy and Steve Waugh have stood behind their struggling captain, Mark Taylor, following his lengthy run of outs. Both players agreed with their captain that he should not demote himself to this weekend's Sheffield Sield match, but rather concentrate on the upcoming one-day match against the West Indies. Page 88.

Promising Australian golfer Robert Allenby may miss The Australian Masters next month because of a dispute over appearance money. Allenby, who may play in South Africa during the week of the Open, is upset at the money being paid to American sensation Tiger Woods to lure him to play in the Open. Page 86.

American tennis player Jennifer Capriati has continued her successful comeback after making the quarter finals of the Sydney International at Kooyong yesterday. The controversial 20-year-old, who has recently comeback from a two-year break from the circuit, says it is still too early to compare her form to that of when she was a teenage star. Page 85.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Racehorse owners have got tough on striking jockeys, and have demanded they guarantee their availability or be overlooked for races during the next month. Owners are also considering a proposal to change the owner-jockey relationship, which would see jockeys paying for rides in big races. Page 80.

The Australian cricket team got a chance to forget their recent poor form as they entertained an enthusiastic crowd at a charity match in Port Arthur yesterday. The day raised money for the victims of the Port Arthur massacre and was welcomed by players as a chance to inject some joy into the recovering community. Page 78.

American athletics champion, Carl Lewis is to race in a grand prix meet in Sydney in January. Lewis, who has been to Australia three times but has never raced, will run in the 100m at Homebush, in what will be his one and only appearance on an Australiantrack. Page 75.
